captions.detailed: A De Dion rear suspension assembly featuring a curved, rigid black tube beam that connects two wheel hubs on either side. Each wheel hub consists of a dark grey brake disc and a light grey stepped cylinder axle, both of which are designed to rotate on continuous revolute joints. Positioned separately in the center is a dark grey differential housing with lateral flanges hosting two short, stepped driveshaft stubs that also rotate independently on revolute joints.
captions.instruction: Generate a De Dion rear axle assembly. It should feature a curved black rigid beam connecting two wheel hubs, each with spinning brake discs and axles on revolute joints, and a central independent differential housing with two short, rotatable driveshaft stubs.
captions.factory: The code constructs a De Dion axle assembly by first creating a rigid beam part using a series of swept or boolean-joined cylinders and boxes to form the curved tube, end mounts, and structural brackets. It then models the wheel hubs as a combination of thin flat cylinders for brake discs and stepped cylinders for the axles. Finally, the differential housing is modeled as a central hub (composed of overlapping cylinders and boxes) with lateral stepped cylinders representing the driveshaft stubs. Revolute joints are configured to link the wheel hubs to the beam ends, and the driveshaft stubs to the housing flanges.
